newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle Columbia lands after mission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle Columbia lands after mission.

text.p: The space shuttle Columbia ended its science mission, curtailed by a malfunctioning power generator, with a safe landing on Tuesday at NASA's Florida spaceport.
The $2 billion gliding spaceship soared through wispy clouds and touched down at the Kennedy Space Centre at 2:33 p.m. EDT (1833 GMT), less than four days after blasting off.
NASA ordered Columbia and its crew of seven home early because one of its three electricity generators had degraded and could have sparked a fire or explosion. The mission was to have lasted 16 days.
The shuttle's laboratory was shut down earlier on Tuesday, with only a tiny fraction of the astronauts' $84 million research programme accomplished.
Scientists have requested a rerun of the mission, which was to have studied the behaviour of fire in space, the growth of plants and the structure of proteins.
It was only the third time a shuttle mission had been cut short by mechanical trouble.
